value.definition: an index from a page to the pages naming it
value.name: edge

invariants.statement: An edge file is found by target id then source property then source page id.
An edge is filed under the target's id whichever identifier the source wrote.
A leaf is named for the source's id.
A page's identity is its id and its slug and the page type its slug is unique within.
A page's identity files no edge.
A name held as a page's identity refuses nothing.
A page stating no `id` refuses nothing.
The identity index files a page's identity.
A name reaching no page files no edge.
A name for a mortal page type refuses nothing.
A name held by a mortal page refuses nothing.
One write creates and removes only files that write alone owns.
A edge free to name more than one page type has the page type in its value.
A edge nested in a record files an edge from its page rather than from its entry.
A edge nested one record deep is reached.
A edge nested deeper than one record is not reached.
A edge in an entry row files an edge from the row's page rather than from the row.
A edge an entry row states is reached.
A edge nested in a record inside an entry row is not reached.
The rows are handed in rather than read here.

value.definition: an index from an identifier to the page with it
value.name: identity

invariants.statement: An identity file is found by unique kind then scope then property then value.
A page unique across every page is filed under no scope.
A scope is a page type or a property's value under a page type.
Only the `page` page type declares an identifier unique across every page.
A line has the page's path and its id.
A slug reaches an id without opening the page.
A page's identifiers are the properties its own page type has stating a `unique`.
An identifier's value is read from a page by the key its property states.
An identifier's value is read as text or as a number.
A file has one line for each page with the value.
A scope no page is filed under has no directory.
No two pages have one slug inside the scope that slug's property declares.
A page with an identifier another page already has does not land.

value.definition: an index from a file to the files importing it
value.name: import

invariants.statement: An import file is named for the path imported.
A line has the path of the file importing the path imported.
Only a body named `.ts` or `.tsx` makes an edge.
A relative specifier makes an edge.
A specifier naming a package makes an edge at the file the naming handed in resolves to.
A specifier the naming handed in does not resolve makes no edge.
A specifier landing outside the repository makes no edge.
What edges a body makes is answered here rather than worked out again by a caller.
A type-only import makes the same edge as any other import.
An edge is filed for the path the body spells whether or not the file that body names stands.

value.definition: an index from what a function says to the files spelling it
value.name: rule

invariants.statement: A said file is named for the digest of the rule that file answers.
A line has the path, the place in that path, and the name spelling the rule.
The place is the count of rules that path spells before this one.
Only a body named `.ts` or `.tsx` spells a rule.
A function only passing names along spells no rule.
A rule string comes from the module reading rules rather than from here.
A path read for rules is filed whether or not that path spells one.
That filing is what says the index has read a path rather than passed it over.
A reader trusts the whole map where today's reader filed it.
A reader asks of no path whether the index has read that path.
A map no reader of today's body filed is all of it suspect and read by none.
A rule a file spells is a function of that file's body and of the reader.
A rebuild files which reader spelled the rules that rebuild filed.
That reader is named by what the reader spells for the reader's own body.
A landing files no reader, one landing refiling one path rather than the map.
A map another reader filed is not whole however many paths were read.
A map naming no reader is not whole.
A reader that changed leaves the map to be filed again rather than read.
No reader is named by a number someone keeps by hand.
A parse moving no rule in the reader's own body is not answered for here.
A reader answers the paths for one rule ordered by path and then by place.
That order is the order a read over the index's paths would spell them in.

value.definition: an index from a page type to the shape of what it carries and of what it is
value.name: shapes

invariants.statement: A shape file is found by the page type whose properties that file has.
A file has one line for each property that page type carries.
What a page type carries is filed apart from what a page property is.
A page property's own shape is filed under the page type that property is.
A page property is filed there whether or not any page type declares it.
A shape filed there says what the property's own page says and nothing more.
Every page property's shape is each of those files read.
A page stating no property slug is filed there nowhere.
A page type carries what it declares and what every page type above it declares.
A line carries the property worked out whole, so a reader reads no second page.
What a page type carries is one file read however many properties it has.
A property is filed under every page type carrying that property.
A property that changes refiles every page type carrying that property.
A page type that changes refiles every page type extending that page type.
A page type carrying no property has no file.
Nothing filed here says which pages are of a page type.

value.definition: an index from a page type to the values its pages have
value.name: value

invariants.statement: A value file is found by the page type whose pages the value file has.
A line has the page's path and the whole value its body declares.
A file has one line for each page of its page type.
Every value a page of one page type carries is one file read.
A page stating no page type is filed here by nothing.
A value standing in a file beside a page is not filed here.
Nothing filed here says which pages name a page.
